sources.title: Ghost of Tsushima: Legends anime delayed to 2028
sources.text: The anime series based on the Sucker Punch Productions -developed PlayStation game Ghost of Tsushima: Legends , which was previously planned to debut in 2027, which will now premiere on Crunchyroll in 2028, Aniplex and Crunchyroll announced . Mayumi Saco and Shinya Fukumatsu will join the cast of the show in undisclosed role. Saco previously voiced Tomoe in the original game, while while Fukumatsu is known for portraying Bomb in One-Punch Man . The anime is being directed by Takanobu Mizuno at studio Kamikaze Douga, with Gen Urobuchi writing the story composition and co-writing the script with Renji Oki. New staff members include composer Keiji Inai, sound director Yoshikazu Iwanami, sound editor Yasumasa Koyama, and title calligraphy artist Gyousyou Suzuki. Ghost of Tsushima: Legends is produced by HAYATE in collaboration with Aniplex and PlayStation Productions, with Sony Music serving as music and soundtrack partner.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Ghost of Tsushima anime arrives in 2028 as OG game actor joins cast
sources.text: Ghost of Tsushima Legends has been delayed The upcoming Ghost of Tsushima anime has received a disappointing release date update alongside news of new cast and behind-the-scenes arrivals. At New York Comic Con, Crunchyroll revealed that Ghost of Tsushima Legends is now set for 2028, a slight pushback from its original 2027 window. Two actors, Mayumi Skco and Shinya Fukumatsu, were also confirmed to join the cast. If you've played Ghost of Tsushima in Japanese, you may recognize Saco's voice – she portrayed turncoat villain Tomoe in 2020's Ghost of Tsushima game. It is unknown who the pair will be portraying in Legends, however. Ghost of Tsushima is a 2020 open world adventure charting the revenge journey of Jin Sakai on the Japanese island of Tsushima during feudal times. It was followed up in 2024 by Ghost of Yotei, offering players a new quest as the katana-wielding Atsu hunted down the fearsome Yotei Six after the murder of her parents. In truth, we probably should have expected the delay. We've heard precious little about Ghost of Tsushima Legends since its announcement way back in January 2025. "The Ghost of Tsushima anime will offer fans an exciting new way to experience the game in an anime style that will be bold and groundbreaking," Crunchyroll president Rahul Purini, said at the time in a statement. PlayStation Productions head Asad Qizilbash added, "Ghost of Tsushima’s rich, immersive world and its fantastical Legends mode based on Japanese mythology provide the perfect canvas for this project, and Aniplex is the perfect partner to translate Sucker Punch Productions’ hit video game into a stunning new anime series." sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film reportedly in development, with CD Projekt Red collaborating with Paramount to make it
sources.text: UPDATE 12PM BST: CD Projekt Red seems to have confirmed the partnership and film, with joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski commenting on X that: "We're excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise. We look forward to sharing more details at the appropriate time." ORIGINAL STORY 11:40AM BST: A live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film is reportedly in the works at Paramount Pictures. Producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura - a former Warner Bros. exec influential in signing the The Matrix and Harry Potter films, and known for producing the Transformers films - is said to be attached to the project, with CD Projekt Red collaborating. The report comes from Deadline , though the publication had no further information to share than what's above. CD Projekt Red told us it doens't have anything to share beyond what Nowakowski said on X. Believing that CD Projekt Red would venture into live-action film territory doesn't take a stretch of the imagination. The company's Netflix anime partnership on Cyberpunk Edgerunners has been a success, with a second series due to air this month, on 20th October . The first season, released in 2022, was "fantastic", Wes wrote in his Cyberpunk Edgerunners impressions article , and amassed considerable Netflix viewing figures . Live-action adaptations of video game-based series are also becoming increasingly popular, with The Last of Us and Fallout particularly finding wide success. CD Projekt Red being involved with the Cyberpunk 2077 adaptation would also somewhat heal a wound left by not being involved with The Witcher Netflix adaptation. CD Projekt art director Pawel Mileniczuk called this a "missed opportunity" when I talked to him for a Witcher 3 10-year anniversary article last year. Meanwhile, CD Projekt Red is working on Cyberpunk 2 , a project that's in pre-production, but with an expanding team - close to 200 people as of 31st July 2026 - full production doesn't seem far away. The sequel apparently adds a second city alongside the iconic Night City setting, and it's described as being like "Chicago gone wrong". Should the live-action film prove real, and be made, the questions are what story will it tell - the same as in Cyberpunk 2077? - and which actors will play the game's well-known roles? The most famous of those roles is Keanu Reeves' portrayal of Johnny Silverhand, a character who used Reeves' likeness in the game. Could Reeves star in a film adaptation? Cyberpunk 2077 was released in 2021 , and its rocky launch has since become infamous. But CD Projekt Red did extensive work improving the game after release, focusing its efforts around a kind of 2.0 relaunch alongside the game's "remarkable" Phantom Liberty expansion , in 2023. Paramount, meanwhile, recently acquired Warner Bros., and has since reorganised into mega-company Skydance. Activision's former leader Bobby Kotick has been employed on the board of it .

sources.title: After Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Daredevil star Charlie Cox is in a new Sega game
sources.text: After dipping his toes into gaming with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Daredevil star Charlie Cox says he's working on an upcoming Sega game. After over 20 years of acting, Cox finally made his game debut in 2025's Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 as lead character Gustave. And despite only spending four hours working on the French JRPG (or J'RPG if you will), the game blew up and unexpectedly became one of his most beloved roles in the long acting career. On top of that, the Cox noted that the game "has seemingly opened a new avenue for my professional work" as he confirmed he was working on another game earlier this year. At New York Comic Con 2026, Cox spoke to IGN (below) and revealed a little more about his upcoming game, explaining, "I did another one, it doesn't have a name yet," and revealing that "I did a Sega one." He adds: "It hasn't come out yet but it was fun to do." Cox continues, "It's hard. It's a whole different job," explaining, "I had to do, like, 40 hours," which is obviously a bit more intensive than his four hours on Clair Obscur. With it not even having a name, naturally details are scarce, but Cox shares an amusing anecdote that maybe shines a bit more light on the game. "I showed up for the first day, and I was like, 'Hi guys, nice to meet you! How are you?' And all of them went, '...oh, he's English.'" He adds, "they wanted him to be American, but like, now I've got to do 40 hours of lines I've not prepared in an accent." It being so early that it doesn't have a name yet means it's probably something we don't even know about; which is to say RPG fans hoping for Cox to bless Persona 6 with a performance are probably out of luck. Given how much RGG Studio loves casting celebrity actors, I can imagine the studio casting Cox in an upcoming game. With Cox having an American accent in Daredevil, a TV show where he plays a lawyer, I'd maybe have to speculate that perhaps a return of the Judgment series could be in the cards? A year later, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Daredevil star Charlie Cox has finally played the hit J'RPG: "I'm not very good at it." Scott has been freelancing for over four years across a number of different gaming publications, first appearing on GamesRadar+ in 2024. He has also written for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, VG247, Play, TechRadar, and others. He's typically rambling about Metal Gear Solid, God Hand, or any other PS2-era titles that rarely (if ever) get sequels. sources.name: Xbox Wire
sources.title: DMZ — 5 Features to Get Excited for in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s New Mode
sources.text: Call of Duty’s upcoming DMZ mode sounds like it’s shaping up to be something special. Set on the new Hajin map and inspired by the events and locations from Modern Warfare 4 ’s Campaign, this open-world combat environment will challenge you to loot, complete objectives, fight both enemies and rival Operators, and extract before everything you’ve earned is lost. Recent intel drops on the official Call of Duty Blog have given us a much clearer picture of what awaits in Hajin when DMZ launches as part of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . Players who have digitally pre-ordered or pre-purchased Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 can gain Early Access to the game’s Campaign starting Friday, October 16 and all of DMZ starting Tuesday, October 20. The events within DMZ are set after the main MW4 Campaign, leaving a power vacuum in its wake. Now it’s up to you to identify a new, mysterious threat and dismantle its operations across the DMZ through various deployments. From scavenging for crafting materials and experimenting with new technology, to leveling up an Operator, the mode sounds like it offers plenty to look forward to. Here are five features to get excited for when you begin your deployment. The 3D Printer will be available back at the Forward Operating Base (FOB) between deployments and will serve as your primary crafting station to build equipment and upgrades for your loadout before you drop into Hajin. The Call of Duty Blog shares that , as you progress through the DMZ, you’ll unlock new crafting recipes to create more powerful equipment – as well as upgrades to the 3D Printer and even the Forward Operating Base itself. Recipes can also be found on deployments and, presuming you extract in one piece, you can then craft those items for your Operator back at the FOB. When focused on crafting new equipment, the two key things you’ll be looking for when looting on deployments will be Resources and 3D Printer Ingredients – these are the two types of main elements to craft all items. There are four basic Resources to find during a deployment: Synthetics, Electronics, Chemicals, and Metals, automatically broken down from looted items, into your Backpack and Stash. 3D Printer Ingredients are rarer materials found in specific areas of Hajin and are valuable as an ingredient to make a new Item. Examples include Binding Catalyst, Biomaterials, Detonators, and Control Units, to name a few. Once you have enough of these two types of materials, you can select how many copies of an item you want to craft at once, then choose where crafted items go: send completed items directly to your Stash for later or equip them directly to your Operator to quickly prepare for the next deployment. Having this flexibility in how you want to engage the enemy during your deployment can open a variety of experiences in DMZ and can make each deployment feel like it matters, even if you come back to the FOB with zero kills to your name – at least you’ve got handful of electronics or a comms module to make it worth your time. Extraction shooters are always more engaging when every deployment has a clear purpose. That’s not going to be problem with DMZ as it will offer three ways to deploy: Story Missions, Dynamic Operations, and Free Roam. Of those, Story Missions and Dynamic Operations are two that really stand out with their defined objectives and high-tier rewards. According to the Call of Duty Blog , Story Missions will feature narrative-led deployments that you can complete and replay, though some remain locked until prerequisites are met. Each entry provides briefing intel, required objectives, and rewards – usually high-value gear and DMZ Cash – along with options for a random mission and additional milestone rewards. Dynamic Operations, meanwhile, give squads multiple goals to pursue within the DMZ. After deploying, you choose an operation and complete its objectives to earn DMZ XP, Cash, and the ability to call in a Supply Drop filled with unpredictable loot. That extra payoff adds anticipation to every successful Op while making Dynamic Operations a promising source of both Cash and XP. Persistent Operators may be DMZ’s most exciting feature because they allow Hajin to leave a lasting mark on you. You’ll begin with two Operator slots, and unlock a third as you progress through DMZ levels. Each Operator then grows stronger by surviving deployments and earning DMZ XP. Each successful exfil levels up your Operator’s Dog Tags, and this is the key to gaining Trait Points for your Operator. You can invest those points across the Warfighter, Scout, and Survivalist Trait Trees, creating a meaningful choice between specialization and flexibility: with a maximum of 18 points to earn, and a choice of over 60 Trait Points to augment your Operator, you can tailor each Operator to your skills and preferred role. For example, Warfighter Traits include Combat Resistance, Quick Fix, and Viper Sense; Scout Traits include improved Thermal Padding, UAV Upgrade, and Field Crafting; while Survivalist Traits include Faster and Free Revives, increased Consumable Duration, and many more. But here’s where it gets dicey: if an Operator fails to extract and becomes MIA, you must either recover them with DMZ Cash or dismiss them. Because recovery costs rise with Trait investment, bringing back a high-level Operator becomes increasingly expensive. Recovered Operators keep their Traits but lose their gear, putting real weight behind every deployment. The chase for loot is at the heart of every extraction shooter, and DMZ makes each haul matter beyond the current deployment. Returning to base with a pack full of supplies doesn’t just feel rewarding – it improves your chances of success the next time you enter Hajin. Once you drop into a deployment, looting should be a top priority. Searching containers provides resources for combat, supports marked Operations, strengthens your position in Hajin, and offers a reliable way to earn DMZ XP and adva

sources.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Launch Rollout Adds DMZ Early Access
sources.text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month. Activision and Infinity Ward revealed a host of new details for its DMZ revamp in a blog post shared today. Early access for the mode joins campaign early access , with both available to those who pre-ordered either the standard or Vault Edition versions of the game across PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and/or Xbox Series X/S. Here's the full breakdown: Eligible players will gain early access to the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign starting Friday, October 16. DMZ early access will then follow Tuesday, October 20, with the full launch unleashing the rest of the experience come Friday, October 23. All of the new details arrived with a new gameplay trailer for DMZ, which you can see below. DMZ was first introduced as Call of Duty's take on the extraction shooter experience with 2022's Modern Warfare 2 . It was expanded upon in the months that followed but was ultimately deemed to be an underwhelming prototype by many. Support ended in late 2023, and now, Activision is taking another swing at it. The DMZ in Modern Warfare 4 has been propped up as a fully fleshed-out evolution for the game mode. In today's post, Infinity Ward described the new take on the mode as the series' "definitive extraction shooter experience," promising persistent progression in the open-world combat environment known as the Hajin Exclusion Zone. "There's an interesting story with the DMZ beta, where we had to make some decisions," studio multiplayer creative director Joe Cecot said in a recent behind-the-scenes video (below). "Certain things we wanted to do, we couldn't do. At the end of the day, we learned a lot: That we made a very approachable, fun sandbox that was fun to fight in, to explore, to make friends in, to get into fights in. There's a bunch of stuff we left on the table, so as soon as we finished with the last game, we were just gung-ho on, 'OK, we know what we want to do.'" Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches October 23 for PC and consoles. Our first proper look at DMZ gameplay arrived in June, with even more details shared earlier this week. While early access players will get to dive into DMZ and the story mode a few days earlier than others, core multiplayer offerings won't officially launch until that firm release date hits. You can see how the team at Infinity Ward is working to deal with wall-hack cheaters here . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. stories.title: Hellraiser: Revival review
stories.summary: How do you revive a series like Hellraiser? When your source material spans four decades and multiple mediums, all with wildly differing tones (and fans), what stays, what goes? sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Hellraiser: Revival review
sources.text: How do you revive a series like Hellraiser? When your source material spans four decades and multiple mediums, all with wildly differing tones (and fans), what stays, what goes? Where would you even begin? It's a question developer Saber Interactive seems to struggle with throughout Hellraiser: Revival and the result is a messy, uneven, but earnest, and often fascinating sort of tribute that, boldly, goes back to the start. Clive Barker's 1986 novella The Hellbound Heart, the genesis of the Hellraiser series, is a queer horror classic; a story of obsession and addiction, loosely inspired by the gay BDSM scene. Later Hellraiser movies would see the series devolve into silliness, iconic villain Pinhead (played by Doug Bradley, who briefly returns here) becoming a quipping counterpart to the Freddies and Chuckies of the time. But Saber seems to have more literary ambitions, drawing heavily on Barker's original themes for its tale of two lovers and their encounter with the Cenonbites; extradimensional beings from a realm where agony and ecstasy are interwined. It's a story that starts with sweaty softcore sex and soon descends into flesh-ripping violence, setting protagonist Aiden against a quasi-religious, extreme BDSM cult as he desperately attempts to rescue his girlfriend Sunny back from Hell. Unfortunately, their relationship is so immediately toxic, it's hard to get emotionally invested in this critical narrative throughline. Tonally, Hellraiser is a strange game. Instead of artfully orchestrated scares, Revival's horrors rely on a grim procession of fused and rended flesh, as relentless as it is effectively offputting. But the ceaseless bodily destruction sits awkwardly alongside villains so deliriously flamboyant, they'd be twiddling their moustaches if it weren't for their masks. And attempts at eroticism and sensuality quickly short circuit amid the dildo-strewn nightclub neon, where extras spit out porn-calibre line readings of flat innuendo. Narratively, it's also a bit of a mess; too obvious and too incoherent by turns, clumsily walking through a minefield of complex ideas - most obviously, the intersection of sex and violence - with all the subtly and nuance of a double-A FPS with an interactive paddle spanking scene. But to its credit, it just about manages to avoid feeling exploitative, and there is, I think, an earnestness to Revival that carries it through. This is the work of a studio, you sense, with a genuine love of the source material - and a desire to do it justice too. And that manifests in a game willing to take some unexpectedly big swings. They don't always work, but at least it's interesting. Take combat, for instance. Revival is, foundationally at least, a fairly bog standard FPS, and it's not long before an early dalliance with perfunctory stealth makes way for more confrontational action. You start with a pistol and, slowly, your arsenal swells to include a shotgun, a revolver, an SMG, and more; an enigmatic old woman intermittently setting up stall to sell you new toys and upgrades (it's not the only time Revival feels like it's channeling Resident Evil 4 ). Eventually, you're mowing down the Unworthy armed with laser-sight pointers and incendiary shells, which should be the absolute antithesis of horror, but Saber just about makes it work. For starters, Aiden moves with a satisfying sense of physicality. He wobbles when he runs, sidesteps with weighty momentum, and, when the melee weapons come out, he bludgeons and slices with sickeningly tangible abandon. And while Revival is undoubtedly action-heavy, Saber still finds tension in withholding. Weapons break, ammo is short, and even the most basic enemies take a good few hits to bring down. Throw in armoured foes which need to be stripped first - either with a swing of something heavy or a particularly aggressive blast - and every combat encounter feels like it's perpetually teetering on the brink of disaster. But Revival strikes a good balance between stressful and unduly punishing. And while I don't love the modern day proliferation of crafting systems, the focus on furious scavenging here feels additive. It heightens the sense of last-gasp desperation as you pocket anything and everything, in the hope you've got enough to eke out a couple more health packs or bullets when things go wrong. Your limited inventory space, meanwhile, forces some tough choices as you frantically shuffle, stash, or abandon items, optimistically Tetrising together the most effective arsenal from the scraps at your disposal. Later, Hellraiser's iconic puzzle box - here, the Genesis Configuration - essentially becomes a gravity gun, so you can fling sawblades, spikes, even fireballs, shredding through multiple bodies as one. And if you're short on the Suffering needed to power it, near-dead enemies wobble on their last legs so you can gruesomely syphon it out of them. Combat's pilfered parts might feel Resident Evil by way of Half-Life and Doom, but at its best, Hellraiser finds an enjoyably ad hoc rhythm of its own - creating showdowns of pure frantic panic as you scramble to juggle weapons that seem to empty their ammo in seconds, as you furiously scan your surroundings for something pointy to use as a projectile, and delve into your inventory, desperately jettisoning stuff to make space for whatever feels most pressing right now. The trouble is Revival spends a lot of time failing to make the most of its tools. Particularly in the first half of the game, progress feels like a linear sequence of encounters that are over before they've even begun, so quick to wrap up there's no space to settle into anything like a rewarding combat rhythm. (Conversely, bosses tend to drag on a touch too long.) And it tends to make for a lot of uninspiring busywork in a game that's already erratically paced, often adopting the relaxed meandering of a walking sim. sources.title: YouTuber Gets Banned For Hellraiser: Revival Censored Gameplay Video That Still Violated ‘Sex And Nudity Policy’
sources.text: Hellraiser: Revival is not afraid to go there . Like the Clive Barker horror series its based on, the survival horror game has all manner of gore, violence, and sex. And now a YouTuber’s been banned over the gameplay they uploaded to their channel from it. The gameplay in question apparently even had black boxes covering up the actual NC-17 stuff. French content creator J0nathan shared the ban notice from YouTube on X (via IGN ). It stated that his channel was removed from the Google-owned platform for violating its policies against sex and nudity. âExplicit content thatâs meant to be sexually gratifying isnât allowed on YouTube,â the ban read. Hellraiser features full nudity at points, including the beginning of the game, so you might think this is not surprising, but J0nathan told IGN that these parts of the video were censored with black bars. sources.title: Following Nintendo and Sony's lead, Xbox is setting up a division exclusively dedicated to movies and non-games partnerships
sources.text: Today, Microsoft announced it is setting up a new branch of the Xbox business named XP. In a blog over at the Xbox Wire, Microsoft details what this new area of the business looks like - it consists of four branches: Xbox Places, Xbox Pictures, Xbox Partnerships, Xbox Products. "[XP] brings together capabilities that have existed across various teams at Xbox for years and aligns them behind a shared mission: helping our franchises reach more people, create deeper connections with players and new fans, and unlock new opportunities for these fandoms to grow around the world," says a press release from Matthew Ball, chief strategy officer at Xbox. "Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of Xbox. XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love." A large focus of Microsoft's newest investment will be in cross-media partnerships, looking particularly at film and TV. It seems lots of publishers are eyeing up the film industry, no doubt buoyed by the massive success of titles like the Super Mario Bros. and Super Mario Galaxy movies ( which have earned $1.36bn and $1bn, respectively ) and Sony's recently released Resident Evil movie (which is tracking at $280m+ at the time of writing). Xbox has had its own notable successes on the big screen, too: last year A Minecraft Movie amassed more than $550m (£415m) in two weeks , immediately setting up a sequel . Xbox has also experimented with TV in the past, too. Fallout is the highlight for the company at the moment, with Fallout Season 2 boasting 83 million viewers tuning in during its first 13 weeks of release . Less successful was Paramount's divisive Halo TV show, which was cancelled after two seasons . A question that springs to my mind when reading this is: where will we go next? There are plenty of Xbox franchises that'd make for good TV; Perfect Dark, Fable, and maybe even a Forza story in the style of Sony's peculiar Gran Turismo show would work. I know the initial run at a Halo TV show was a bit of a flop, but I'd love to see a limited series on the Fall of Reach. It'd make some fine prestige television. We know there's a Gears of War film and a Sea of Thieves film in production, too. Elsewhere, there's Xbox Places. This is the arm of the company that'll oversee the Minecraft theme parks that are opening in the US and UK that so far represent over £85m of investment from Mojang and Xbox. They're expected to open 'between 2026 and 2027'. Will we hear about more real-life locations that'll fall under the 'Places' banner? It remains to be seen. All these initiatives will no doubt require staffing, which is such to be a sore subject for any of the staff that have been impacted by wide-ranging cuts at Microsoft and Xbox over the past few years . Given the contraction of its game studios and software business, is Xbox trying to recoup costs by pursuing other avenues for growth? It certainly seems like it.

sources.title: NBA 2K27 tops US August charts, becomes third-best selling game of 2026 | US Monthly Charts
sources.text: New games dominated the Top 5, including Madden NFL 27, Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, EA's Kickoff bundle, and Star Wars: Zero Company NBA 2K27 topped the US charts in August, becoming the third-best-selling game of the year according to Circana data. Released into early access on August 26, NBA 2K27 reached the top spot in four days of Circana's tracking period, which ran from August 2 to August 29. This follows news earlier this week that NBA 2K25 is set to be delisted from storefronts at the end of the month , with servers taken offline on December 31, 2026. Six new releases made the Top 10 best-selling games in August, including Madden NFL 27 in second place, followed by Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls in third. New games dominated the Top 5, with Electronic Art's Kickoff bundle (which includes the standard editions of Madden NFL 27 and EA Sports College Football 27) in fourth and Star Wars: Zero Company from Respawn Entertainment in fifth place. FromSoftware's Elden Ring jumped 34 places to No.7 following the release of its Nintendo Switch 2 version on August 28. Total consumer spend on video games fell 9% in the US in August to $4.3 billion, mainly due to an 18% drop in mobile revenue. Monopoly Go, Royal Match, and Candy Crush Saga climbed into the top three games for August, with Pokemon Go dropping four places to No.7 after its 10th anniversary celebrations ended, which generated $48.5 million, according to AppMagic estimates . Total content sales dropped 10% to $3.8 billion, down from $4.1 billion in August 2025. Console content fell 7% YoY, while subscription spending grew 3% and PC increased 13% YoY. Circana found that year-to-date spending on new physical software increased 5% in August to $738 million. Spending on Game-Key Card physical releases rose 631%, offsetting a 3% drop in other physical media. Hardware unit sales fell 15% year-on-year to 559,000, the lowest August total since 2013, when it was 423,000 units. Xbox hardware unit sales declined 31% to the lowest August total since 2020, while PlayStation fell 11% to its lowest August total since 2013. Nintendo hardware sales decreased 15% compared to August 2025. Overall hardware spending dropped 3% to $302 million. However, PlayStation 5 hardware sales grew 17% year-over-year. Growth was offset by 13% spending drops across Xbox Series and Switch 2 hardware. Circana also noted that the average price for a new unit of gaming hardware in the US reached an August record of $541. The previous August record was $476 last year. sources.title: Trainwatch launches March 10, 2027
sources.text: Time management mystery adventure game Trainwatch will launch for PC via Steam on March 10, 2027, publisher 11 bit studios and developer Harvester Games announced. “ Trainwatch might be the most mechanics-heavy of my games, but the gist of psychological horror is still very much there, and underlies everything,” said solo developer Rem Michalski in a press release. “It’s a more nuanced kind of horror than explicit violence and jump scares. It’s about an unsettling experience, a claustrophobic setting, and internal, human traumas.” Here is an overview of the game, via 11 bit studios: In Trainwatch , you’ll experience the rush of memorizing the train timetable and closing and raising the gate. You’ll also have to keep an eye on your hunger meter, get a good amount of sleep, and make sure to keep your hands washed after any bathroom breaks so you don’t get sick. As you progress, you’ll unlock new skills and abilities, all the while being drawn further and further into the fog surrounding the Tower. Strangers ask for help or a conversation, incoming trains carry messages, and the weirdness spins faster and faster. But be warned, the clock keeps ticking: a day can’t be stretched, and not every lead can be chased, or every promise kept. If you want to fix your life in a month, you’ll need to decide what matters most and learn to let go.
